title: Portrayal NOS overlay (v0) — joins a NOS's naming/entity tree onto physical IDs

interfaces.description: logical interface naming rules; {n} expands over a group's rel-pos

name.description: NOS interface name pattern, e.g. 'swp{n}' or 'Ethernet{(n-1)*4}'

entity-map.description: rules joining NOS component names (ENTITY-MIB / ietf-hardware / OpenConfig) to physical ids or regions; NOS trees are joined, never drawn; unmapped NOS nodes are legal

source.description: which tree these names come from; omit = any

match.description: NOS component name pattern, e.g. 'sfp{n}' or 'PSU-{n}'

identity.description: WHAT THIS DEVICE IS SOLD AS when it runs this NOS. Optional, and its absence is meaningful: an overlay without it is a naming and mapping layer over somebody else's hardware, which is what every overlay was until this field existed. With it, the overlay also declares a distinct orderable thing whose vendor is the SOFTWARE house - IP Infusion sells OcNOS on a whitebox, and the buyer's asset register says IP Infusion even though Edgecore made the metal. The hardware is never duplicated. The device is modelled once, the overlay carries only what the software changes, and the DCIM export files the result under this vendor instead of the manufacturer of record. OPT-IN ON PURPOSE, because emitting one device type per (device x NOS) multiplies entries in a DCIM: two overlays is nothing, a whitebox fleet times four NOSes is a combinatorial jump that should be somebody's decision rather than a side effect.

vendor.description: slug from spec/schemas/vendors.yaml, whose `role` must be software or both. Not the manufacturer of the metal - that is the device's own `manufacturer:` and it does not move when the software changes

model.description: what the software vendor calls this combination. `{model}` expands to the HARDWARE device type's model, which is its SKU - so `ArcOS on {model}` becomes `ArcOS on 7726-32X-O-AC-F`. Use it whenever the hardware has more than one orderable SKU: the AC and 48 V, front-to-back and back-to-front variants are four different things you can buy, and a name that does not distinguish them collapses four device types onto one. Where the software vendor publishes a bundle SKU of their own, that instead - but a model naming only the NOS cannot be told from the same NOS on different metal, and the export appends the hardware model when it would otherwise collide.

part-number.description: the software vendor's orderable part number, where one exists. Often it does not name the hardware at all - DriveNets' numbers do not - which is exactly why the mapping needs recording here rather than being derived

source.description: how this pairing is known: a live `show version`, a vendor compatibility matrix, a quote. Required because a NOS-to-hardware pairing is a fact about what someone sells, it changes, and when the vendor's part numbers do not name the hardware it is knowledge WE derived rather than read
